body.statement: The Gaussian-multiplier band in Definition~\ref{def:multiplier-band} has simultaneous fixed-grid coverage \[\Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in\left[\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K\right]\ \text{for every }1\le j\le J\right\}\to1-\alpha.\] Moreover, with \(\widehat V_R=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\{q^\top(\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i})\}^2\), \[\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),\] so the usual two-sided studentized interval has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).
body.justification: The fixed-grid band needs only positive counterfactual marginal variances, while grid-RMST studentization needs only positive variance in the declared scalar direction; neither requires full joint covariance rank.
body.gap: Westling et al. (2024, Sections 5.2--5.3) calibrate bands and RMST for directly estimated survival curves; no cited work calibrates the transported spectral counterfactual with estimated donor weights and possibly singular cross-coordinate covariance.
body.consumer: TCL investigators can report a familywise-valid untreated survival trajectory and a single treatment-effect interval on the prespecified follow-up grid if the theorem's sampling, learner, transport, and variance conditions are verified.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) denote the counterfactual \(J\times J\) principal blocks of \(\Omega_\eta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\). Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\to_P\Omega_\theta\), even when these matrices are singular. Put \(\sigma_j^2=(\Omega_\theta)_{jj}=\operatorname{Var}(\Phi_{\theta,i,j})\). Assumption~\ref{ass:counterfactual-coordinate-variance} gives
\[
 \min_{1\le j\le J}\sigma_j^2\ge v>0,
 \qquad \widehat\sigma_j\to_P\sigma_j>0.
\]
Thus every division in Definition~\ref{def:multiplier-band} is well defined with probability tending to one; any convention on the complementary event is asymptotically irrelevant.

Conditionally on the sample,
\[
 Z_K^*=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\xi_i\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}
\]
is exactly centered Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\). Its studentized covariance is
\[
 \widehat R_K
 =\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \widehat\Omega_\theta
 \operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \to_P
 R=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \Omega_\theta
 \operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}.
\]
Both \(R\) and \(\widehat R_K\) are positive semidefinite and \(R_{jj}=1\); positive definiteness is not asserted.

Let \(Z\sim\mathcal N_J(0,R)\) and \(H=\max_j|Z_j|\). Each marginal \(Z_j\) is standard normal. For every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 \{H=t\}\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^J\{|Z_j|=t\},
\]
and every event on the right has probability zero. Hence \(H\) is atomless. It is also strictly increasing on its range. Indeed, let \(S=\operatorname{range}(R)\), the support subspace of \(Z\). For \(0\le x_1<x_2\), choose a nonzero \(z_0\in S\) and scale it so that \(x_1<\|z_0\|_\infty<x_2\). The shell
\[
 \{z\in S:x_1<\|z\|_\infty<x_2\}
\]
is then a nonempty relatively open subset of \(S\). The restriction of the Gaussian law to \(S\) has a strictly positive density with respect to Lebesgue measure on \(S\), because \(R\) is positive definite on its range. The shell consequently has positive probability. Thus the distribution function of \(H\) is continuous and strictly increasing, and its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile \(c_{1-\alpha}\) is unique.

The positive-semidefinite square-root map is continuous in fixed dimension. If \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N_J(0,I_J)\), then along every subsequence on which \(\widehat R_K\to R\), a further subsequence converges almost surely and
\[
 \widehat R_K^{1/2}\varepsilon\longrightarrow R^{1/2}\varepsilon
\]
almost surely on the product space. The atomlessness just proved gives convergence of the corresponding conditional distribution functions at every point. Strict increase at the target quantile then gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_Pc_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad P(H\le c_{1-\alpha})=1-\alpha.
\]
This subsequence argument establishes convergence in probability for the original sequence.

On the sampling side, Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, covariance consistency, and the continuous-mapping theorem yield
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J}
 \left|\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)}{\widehat\sigma_j}\right|
 \rightsquigarrow H.
\]
Combining this limit, critical-value consistency, and continuity of the law of \(H\) proves
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K\right]
 \text{ for every }1\le j\le J\right\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} is used to keep \(J\) fixed.

For the scalar grid target, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, the definition \(\tau_R=q^\top(s_1-\theta)\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)
 &=q^\top\sqrt K\{(\widehat s_1-s_1)-(\widehat\theta-\theta)\}\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^Kq^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})+o_P(1)\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}+o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:grid-rmst-variance} gives directly
\[
 V_R=\operatorname{Var}\{q^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})\}\ge v>0.
\]
No lower bound on any other direction of \(\Omega_\eta\) is used. The empirical \(L_2\)-consistency in Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
 \left|\widehat V_R-K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\right|=o_P(1).
\]
Since \(E\Phi_{\tau,i}^2<\infty\), the weak law gives \(K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\to_PV_R\). Hence \(\widehat V_R\to_PV_R>0\). The scalar projection of the joint Gaussian limit and Slutsky's theorem give
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Therefore
\[
 \left[\widehat\tau_R-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K},
 \widehat\tau_R+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K}\right]
\]
has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\). This conclusion concerns the declared fixed-grid functional and not a continuous-time RMST integral.
